w: Kanubhai Amin, a devotee, brought his mentally retarded son, Samir, to be blessed by Swamishri. Then he expressed his anxiety, "Swami, my son does not even know who's puja he does and who is Swaminarayan. How will he be redeemed?" "It will be done. Since he was born in your home, he will be redeemed," Swamishri assured. Then Kanubhai expressed his frustration, "This son of mine is like Jad Bharat." "That's good. You can worship God without any hassle," Swamishri replied. "But what will happen to him when my wife and I die?" Kanubhai asked. "You should not think of that. God is looking after him now and will care for him afterwards. It is He who looks after everyone." Swamishri reassured the devotee that God is the sustainer of all life.
If one remains humble then he will be honored with praises. And if one remains arrogant then people will not love him.
By remaining humble one accomplishes one's work easily.

At 10.00 a.m. In the presence of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, Swamishri told sadhus to chant Vedic mantras while he worshipped the Narmada waters by showering sanctified flowers. When Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami split a coconut and sprinkled its water into the Narmada canal Swamishri responded, "Jai Maharaj. May the waters flow forever and may it reach Saurashtra and Kutch ..."
At 7.00 p.m. The pujan rituals were carried out in a boat amidst Vedic chantings, worship of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and arti by Swamishri and the Chief Minister. ( See special News report )

In the evening assembly, youths performed a wonderful traditional dance on the lyric, "Swaminarayan charan kamalma..." Thereafter Swamishri was honored with garlands, flower shawls and gifts by sadhus and youths. Inspiring incidents of youths in Vadodara Satsang Mandal were then narrated in the assembly. A debate on, "Is Study or Character Greater?" was effectively presented by youths.

Finally, Swamishri blessed the Youth Day assembly, "Character is more important because it endows you with humility, discrimination, the virtue to serve others, to not get angry, to tolerate and to do good. Whereas one who has advanced academically will not be able to tolerate. He will become agitated and angry. We cannot discount studies, however character is the greater of the two ornaments... To run our lives financially and to run our world through the technology we have invented, we need academic studies. But the glory and importance of that lies in having character. It is character that decorates our mundane works..."

Day 2 - National Bal-Balika Shibir 2004 The balaks sang kirtans, recited mukhpath and performed a dance in Swamishri's puja. Swamishri also launched the 'Pramukh Cup', a 7-a-side football tournament, and also pleased a young balak by enticing him to grab the football whilst he continuously moved it in his hands. This little action brought a smile to everyone in the audience. The morning session of the shibir saw senior sadhus speaking on the importance of remembering divine moments with Swamishri on a regular basis.

The balaks then went to play the Pramukh Cup Tournament held at Alperton Goals. From throughout the UK, 42 teams participated in the tournament, which was won by Saturday London Mandir Bal Mandal Team A. In the evening session, Swamishri presented the trophy to the winning team.

Day 2 - National Family Shibir 2004 During the day there were a series of talks and panel discussions on understanding Swamishri's wishes. Yuvaks took niyams to do puja daily, tilak- chandlo regularly and to attend the weekly assembly on time. The final session of the shibir was on the topic of faith in God. Swamishri stressed in his blessings the importance of steadfastly abiding by the principles of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The finale of this shibir was the Fuldol celebration, in which all the yuvaks and balaks were sprayed by Swamishri with the saffron-coloured water sanctified by Shri Harikrishna Maharaj.

Trustees of The Heritage Trust, based in Surat, came for Swamishri’s darshan. They had published a book entitled Sanskruti Purush Pramukh Swami, which had been written for them by Vivekpriya Swami. Mahant Swami performed the inauguration of the book.
